title: Cech cup products and pullback
statement: Let f:X' \to X be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], let U be an arbitrary open cover of X, and let U' be an open cover of X' together with a specified refinement map U' \to f^{-1}U in the sense of Stacks Tag 01FD. Let F and G be quasi-coherent modules on X [pqf-def-coherent], and write f^*F and f^*G for their pullbacks to X' [def-pc-module-pullback]. (a) The refinement cochain map from the Cech complex of (X,U,F) to that of (X',U',f^*F) is compatible with the usual pullback map H^p(X,F) \to H^p(X',f^*F) under the canonical maps from Cech cohomology to cohomology, \check H^p(U,F) \to H^p(X,F) and \check H^p(U',f^*F) \to H^p(X',f^*F), which exist for every open cover. (b) For an arbitrary open cover U of X, the signed Cech cup-product cochain map of Tag 07MB, Tot(Cech(U,F) \otimes Cech(U,G)) \to Cech(U,F\otimes G), induces on cohomology a map \check H^p(U,F) \otimes \check H^q(U,G) \to \check H^{p+q}(U,F\otimes G) that is compatible with the sheaf cup product H^p(X,F) \otimes H^q(X,G) \to H^{p+q}(X,F\otimes G) under the canonical maps \check H^n(U,-) \to H^n(X,-) (Stacks Tag 0FKV, cohomology-lemma-diagrams-commute); in particular, when these canonical maps are isomorphisms (for instance for a finite affine cover of a scheme with affine diagonal and quasi-coherent F, G), the Cech cup product is the sheaf cup product. Both assertions are natural in F,G and f.
